body:
## Identity Paths Change Optimization

A deep plain stack must learn both useful transformations and a route for preserving information. Residual structure supplies the preservation route from the start.

The block represents input plus a learned correction, so zero-like branch outputs begin near an identity mapping. This improves gradient flow and makes adding depth less destructive.

Newer variants change which features are normalized or remove learned shifts for efficiency. Judge them through training stability, final quality, and kernel support rather than name alone.
common_mistakes: Residual connections permanently skip every transformation.
Layer normalization averages unrelated users together.
Normalization removes all learned scale and shift.

real_world_usage: These support stable information and gradient flow through deep transformer stacks.
